citation_scope_note: §12.4 SIXTH THROUGH NINTH INSTANCES, 2026-08-14 — and the cause is this seat's own lesson turned back on it. The citation audit added an hour earlier scanned for CORPUS ids only, because this edition thinks in cards; widened to EVERY repo path cited in a shipped file, it immediately found four more artifacts cited as evidence and never listed (rows below): the typed ACCEPTANCE that makes this edition's own status claim true, the C1 referee pass behind a discharged finding, the routing document a defect claim is measured against, and the Lean import root that the phrase 'in the build cone' is evidence-for. A CHECK INHERITS THE CATEGORIES OF WHOEVER WROTE IT — stated by the Librarian about their own two-shelf sweep, proved here within the hour against the seat that quoted it. DELIBERATELY NOT ROWS, with the reason recorded as §12.4's converse requires: engine/job_gate.py and engine/release_verify.sh are named as PROCEDURE (how a computation was run, who runs the certifier), not cited as documents whose CONTENT warrants a claim — the artefact that warrants is the release log, which is a row. THE TEST THAT SETTLES IT, from the Librarian who reviewed this line rather than let it pass (20260814T145238Z-librarian-9143-289d): IF THE FILE'S CONTENT CHANGED, WOULD ANY CLAIM IN THIS EDITION BECOME FALSE? For the release log, yes. For the gate script, no — a different job_gate would not make a recorded run untrue. And the practical bound: listing procedure paths would drag the whole engine into every edition's checkable set and make the set meaningless by size. The exclusion is recorded rather than silent so it is reviewable as a judgement instead of readable as an omission.

readers_edition.F-E12: RULED — manifest §12.6 (Architect 20260814T124410Z-architect-64561-f666), 'read-but-not-held surfaces'. (1) A redeploy is part of the repair, not a follow-up: any published copy is re-published IN THE SAME ACT that changes a file it renders from, and a repair whose published surface still shows the defect is an UNFINISHED REPAIR. (2) The manifest records the redeploy date beside the URL — a dated measurement like any other row — and the row verifies by regeneration-and-republication. (3) AT DEPOSIT the gate extends one surface outward: every published copy is re-published from the deposited bytes, or RETIRED, within the deposit act itself, so a reader's surface can never outlive the record it renders. The finding as reported: THE COPY UNDER REVIEW IS A SHIPPED SURFACE THAT NO CLAUSE REACHED, and it is the one a reviewer actually reads. §12.2 gates at DEPOSIT; this copy exists to be read BEFORE deposit, which is its whole purpose. §12.4 closes the checkable set under citation and this manifest cites the URL — but a remote page cannot carry a sha, so it cannot be a row in the ordinary way. For four hours after the repair it displayed hashes this seat had already corrected: the record was right and the thing a human was looking at was wrong. Verify by regeneration (§12.3) plus a re-publish whenever the file it renders from changes; the standing rule adopted here is that a redeploy is part of the repair, not a follow-up to it.

anchor_policy.rule: AN EDITION ANCHORS BY CONTENT. The bytes it names must be obtainable from inside the edition or its shipped substrate. A commit reference is PROVENANCE and is never required to verify.
anchor_policy.why: The commit was never needed for IDENTITY. Every row already names its bytes by sha256; the commit named WHERE THE BYTES CAME FROM. The one row that carried a commit pins an APPEND-ONLY JOURNAL whose on-disk hash goes stale by design, so the real requirement was 'a fixed historical state no later wave can move' — and a fixed state is identified by its HASH. Keeping the bytes meets that requirement without making this edition depend on the repository's history, which is a property no edition controls and which the estate changed on 2026-09-11.
anchor_policy.the_cost_of_this_rule_stated_here_becaus: Content-anchoring plus shipped bytes makes a row SELF-ATTESTING: it proves the bytes are the ones this manifest names, and CANNOT prove this manifest was ever right. The cure is not a commit — it is an external archive: a preservation bundle, or a deposit under a persistent identifier. CONTENT FOR RESOLUTION, EXTERNAL ARCHIVE FOR INDEPENDENCE. verify_edition.py prints which of the two a reader is holding, on the line it emits.
